name: H. G. Wells
summary: Wells described himself as a Socialist, favouring gradual, administered public ownership of land and main services, heavy death duties and graduated taxes, and a state that guarantees work. His consistent aim was a federal world state or league with real authority above nations, ending armaments and secret diplomacy, and in 1940 he drafted a universal declaration of human rights. He also wrote early eugenic and race-efficiency proposals and favoured rule by a voluntary, trained elite.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He aimed at disarmament through a world authority, though that authority was to have force.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Utopia's ruling order is not hereditary, because inheritance is "silly" as a basis of rule.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Utopia keeps money, a minimum wage and a tax-funded insurance, and the modern Socialist, he wrote, is not a communist.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: He wanted a Supreme Court of the League of Nations to judge international conflicts.

arms-reduction.rationale: He wrote that the war "aims straight at disarmament" and at a settlement that ends armaments.

central-planning.rationale: In The New World Order he called for world socialism "scientifically planned and directed", as quoted in the scholarly chapter.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He wrote that Britain's rule in Egypt, India and Palestine is justifiable only as trusteeship until the League can act as a public trustee.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He praised Marx for seeing economic development as a process but called his confident class-war generalisation too comprehensive; socialism might arrive by gradual concession.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Socialism, he wrote, trusts competition for fame, service and position, but he wanted peoples united under a world authority and not left to struggle.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He ranked peoples by social efficiency, spoke of inferior races and expected one common language and law to prevail.

death-penalty.rationale: He wrote that in Utopia there would be no killing and even for murder the State would not kill.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Utopia keeps the state as reserve employer, pays pensions and shelters the derelict and sick, and Wells wrote nothing about welfare creating dependency.

decide-locally.rationale: Utopia has great local governments, but they hold their powers under a World State that is sole landowner and sets the common law, and Wells argued for a federal world state controlling money, communications and force.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In 1914 he backed the Allied war effort as a war to end war and German militarism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He opposed class rule and Bolshevik methods, favouring a non-violent liberal socialism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He treated the citizenship and economic independence of women as implications of socialism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He urged a League of Nations with real authority up to a "Parliament of Mankind", and said that association requires some sacrifice of national freedom.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He wrote that the New Republic would let any man into efficient citizenship, white, black, red or brown, and he drafted the 1940 declaration of the rights of man for everyone.

experts-over-public.rationale: Utopian rule rests with the voluntary samurai order and the New Republic is led by able, scientifically trained men, though in 1938 he doubted that specialists form an elite fit to lead.

gradual-change.rationale: He said Socialism may arrive "by the gradual and detailed concession of its propositions" and described steady, methodical transfers of services.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Utopia secludes the insane and those with transmissible disease so they do not become parents, and Anticipations looks to discouraging multiplication of the unfit, though Mankind in the Making doubts that selected persons can yet be barred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Socialism, he wrote, seeks to end the competition to get and hold property so that men compete for service and salaries, and he aimed at abolishing unearned ownership.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Utopian State acts as "the reserve employer of labour", finding work for anyone who wants it at a minimum wage that covers a decent life.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: He regarded the Marxist terminology of surplus value as obsolete and a basis he did not hold.

land-redistribution.rationale: He wanted land owned by the community or world state and leased out, not given to those who farm it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Utopia leaves alcohol to personal conscience short of public drunkenness, but drug-takers who repeat the offence are removed from the free community, so the record points both ways and leans against legal recreational drugs.

limit-population.rationale: Utopia regulates births through marriage and birth laws, and Anticipations says the New Republic would make multiplication of the socially inefficient unpleasant and difficult.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wells wanted competition kept for fame, service and position but not for getting property, and said the New Republic would hold "no superstition of laissez faire".

nation-first.rationale: Wells argued that national independence must give way to a wider association and that patriotic cant keeps nations apart.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He wanted the League's authority to override national sovereignty.

national-self-determination.rationale: He said both self-determination and international control are wanted, and that no large proposition about self-determination meets all cases.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected both unreformed capitalism and Bolshevism for a non-Bolshevik "liberal socialism".

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Utopia provides for formal divorce without disgrace where spouses are incompatible, though adultery ends a marriage as a public offence.

one-party-rule.rationale: He rejected "dictators" and "oligarchic parties" for the world order he wanted.

open-borders.rationale: His Utopia is a world state with one language in which people travel and settle freely, so national borders disappear.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: He expected socialism by gradual concession and orderly change rather than convulsion.

party-controls-media.rationale: The New World Order demanded "the completest freedom of speech, criticism and publication", as quoted in the scholarly chapter.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He argued that a league or super-state must take over part of national sovereignty, saying we cannot have our cake and eat it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wells set aside Marx's surplus-value theory as outmoded terminology and held that owners may be parasitic through speculation and idle property, not that all profit is exploitation.

property-franchise.rationale: Utopian local elections give the vote to every permanent resident over fifteen.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wells wrote that absolute property hardly exists and proposed gradual abolition of the great bulk of private ownership, with land resumed by the community by taxation, purchase and partly compensated confiscation.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He held that property is relative and limited and exists only under conditions the community sets.

public-ownership.rationale: The constructive Socialist works to transfer the main public services steadily from private enterprise to municipal and State control, and in Utopia the roads, railways and energy sources are public.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Utopian franchise covers every permanent resident, with no racial or ethnic bar.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Reporting from America, he described the drift towards stricter social barriers, lynching and denial of education to Black people as a shameful state of affairs.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The New Republic would attack irresponsible property and speculation and treat credit as a human contrivance open to control, rather than leave business unregulated.

rehabilitation.rationale: Utopia would give first offenders and those under twenty-five remedial schooling, but would exile repeat offenders to islands for permanent seclusion.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: In Utopia land and natural energy are the inalienable property of the World State and are leased out for a limited term.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He faulted the early Marxists for crude notions of class action and neglect of the necessities of government, and wanted the state run by an administrative, not class, order.

state-harmful.rationale: His whole programme is a powerful world state, which he saw as the means to peace and welfare.

strong-leader.rationale: Wells wrote "we do not want dictators, we do not want oligarchic parties or class rule", though he also called democratic institutions a slow and slack method.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Anticipations proposes a scheme of death duties and heavy graduated taxes, and New Worlds for Old lists death duties among the means of resuming land for the community.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He proposed death duties and heavy graduated taxes on irresponsible incomes as a main means of controlling great unearned fortunes.

taxation-theft.rationale: He proposed heavy taxation and land resumption as a normal tool of the state, and called the common good the test of any property.

unions-good.rationale: He praised no union as such: Anticipations calls the trade-union spirit a conservative contagion of old craftsmanship, while Utopia lets no union limit a worker, and his socialist writing treats them as part of labour representation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Utopian state shelters and "strengthens" any citizen who is ill, which supports public provision of health care without stating a full universal scheme.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He warned that concentrated property could produce a plutocratic aristocracy ending in imperialism and social disintegration.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wells attacked "vast diffused slums of peasant proprietors" and wanted land held by the community, not spread among small owners.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He listed the economic independence of women among the things socialism must bring.

women-suffrage.rationale: Utopian local elections give the vote to every permanent resident over fifteen, with no exclusion of women.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: He wrote that "work as a moral obligation is the morality of slaves" and that a modern Utopian is free to be idle once he has earned the minimum wage.

notes: Positions are the mature socialist and world-state ones (1901-1940); A Modern Utopia is a description of his proposed ideal society and is used for stated proposals, not for its fiction. Early Anticipations (1901) is franker on race and population than his later work. Themes searched in the local Project Gutenberg corpus: economy and property, taxation, government and suffrage, world and war, religion, family and sex, race, population. Little found on guns, policing, immigration levels, religion in schools, environment, or technology policy.
